intro: For developers who know JavaScript and Node.js basics and want to build web servers and REST APIs with Express 5. You'll go from a first server to routing, middleware, error handling, data, and production practices, using Express 5's current behaviour rather than the Express 4 patterns most older tutorials teach.
assumedKnowledge: Modern JavaScript, including async/await and ES modules or CommonJS
HTTP basics: methods, status codes, headers and JSON

steps.title: Install Express and run your first server
steps.goal: Create a project, install Express 5 and serve a Hello World response.
steps.explanation: Create a folder, run npm init, and install express. A minimal app creates an application with express(), registers a route with app.get('/', handler) and starts listening on a port. Express 5 requires Node.js 18 or newer.
steps.versionNote: Express 5 is the current major version and needs Node.js 18+. Tutorials that pin express@4 teach APIs that Express 5 removed.

steps.title: Route requests to handlers
steps.goal: Define routes for each HTTP method, read route parameters and query strings, and group routes with express.Router.
steps.explanation: A route pairs an HTTP method and a path with one or more handler functions. Use route parameters such as /users/:id to capture values in req.params, and express.Router() to split related routes into their own modules mounted with app.use().
steps.versionNote: Express 5 changed path syntax. Wildcards must be named (/*splat, or /{*splat} to also match the root), optional parameters use braces (/:file{.:ext}) instead of ?, and regular-expression characters in string paths are no longer supported. req.query is read-only and uses the simple parser by default.

steps.title: Understand and write middleware
steps.goal: Explain how middleware functions form a request pipeline, and write your own for logging, auth checks and validation.
steps.explanation: Middleware functions receive req, res and next, and either end the response or call next() to pass control on. Order matters: middleware runs in the order it's registered. Application-level, router-level and built-in middleware all follow the same pattern.

steps.title: Parse request bodies and serve static files
steps.goal: Accept JSON and form submissions with the built-in body parsers, and serve a folder of static files.
steps.explanation: express.json() and express.urlencoded() parse request bodies into req.body, and express.static() serves files such as images and a built front end. No separate body-parser package is needed.
steps.versionNote: In Express 5, express.urlencoded() defaults to extended: false, req.body is undefined (not {}) when nothing was parsed, and express.static() ignores dot-files and dot-directories by default. Older tutorials that install body-parser separately or rely on req.body always being an object are out of date.

steps.title: Use the request and response APIs
steps.goal: Read headers, params and bodies from req, and send JSON, status codes, redirects and files with res.
steps.explanation: The API reference documents every property and method on the application, request, response and router objects. Use res.status(code).json(data) for APIs and res.sendStatus(code) for empty responses.
steps.versionNote: Express 5 removed several old signatures: use res.status(404).json(obj) instead of res.json(obj, 404), res.sendStatus(code) instead of res.send(code), res.redirect(status, url) argument order, res.sendFile instead of res.sendfile, and app.delete instead of app.del. req.param() is gone; read from req.params, req.body or req.query.

steps.title: Handle errors, including in async code
steps.goal: Write an error-handling middleware and let Express forward errors from async handlers to it.
steps.explanation: Error handlers are middleware with four arguments (err, req, res, next) registered after your routes. Respond with a safe message and status, and keep stack traces out of production responses.
steps.versionNote: Express 5 catches rejected promises from async handlers and middleware and passes them to your error handler, so the try/catch-and-next(err) wrappers and express-async-errors package from Express 4 tutorials are no longer needed.

steps.title: Connect a database
steps.goal: Choose a database driver for your app and read and write data from your route handlers.
steps.explanation: Express has no built-in database layer. You add the Node.js driver or library for your database (for example MongoDB, PostgreSQL or Redis) and call it from your handlers, keeping data access in separate modules.

steps.title: Debug and run behind a proxy
steps.goal: Turn on Express's debug logging and configure trust proxy so client IPs and protocols are correct when deployed.
steps.explanation: Set the DEBUG environment variable to see internal routing logs. Most hosting platforms put a proxy or load balancer in front of your app; the trust proxy setting tells Express to read the forwarded client IP and protocol.
steps.versionNote: Router debug namespaces changed in Express 5 from express:router to router.

steps.title: Secure your app
steps.goal: Apply the official security practices: dependency updates, TLS, secure headers, input validation, safe cookies and brute-force protection.
steps.explanation: The security best-practices guide covers using maintained Express versions, serving over TLS, adding secure HTTP headers (for example with Helmet), validating user input, setting cookies securely, and limiting repeated login attempts.

steps.title: Prepare for production
steps.goal: Run Express fast and reliably in production with the right environment settings, logging, process management, health checks and graceful shutdown.
steps.explanation: Set NODE_ENV=production, use compression and async logging, avoid synchronous functions in request handlers, run under a process manager or container restart policy, and handle shutdown signals so in-flight requests finish.
